Mobilizing the world, four paws at a time.
Free mobility service dogs for people with physical disabilities
Illini Service Dogs is a nonprofit and student organization at the University of Illinois. We train mobility service dogs and place them 100% free of charge, funded entirely by donations.
We believe that through community education, advocating for disability rights and providing service dogs 100% free of charge, we are making the world a better place, four paws at a time.

Illini Service Dogs was founded in 2010 at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign by Bridget Evans, inspired by her own service dog, Coal.
ISD is run by three groups: an administrative board, an advisory board, and a student executive board.
ISD is 100% funded by donations. Gifts pay for dog food, vet care, training supplies and toys.

value: ISD places mobility service dogs, 100% free of charge, with people who have physical disabilities and could benefit from a mobility service dog.
[ISD to confirm]

ISD does not go first come, first served, and we don't quote wait times. Each year we match applicants with dogs nearing the end of training, based on each applicant's needs. We encourage you to also apply to other service dog programs.
Apply: Fill out ISD's online application.
Review: The ISD team reviews your application.
Waitlist: Approved applicants join the waitlist.
Matching: Each year, ISD matches applicants with dogs nearing the end of training.
Placement: You and your new service dog begin working together.

Puppy raisers care for an ISD dog in training in their own home. Our dogs are in the program from about 8 weeks to 2.5 years old, and a placement usually lasts 2 to 6 months. Puppy raisers must live in the Champaign-Urbana area.
UIUC students can join ISD as members. We recruit new members in the fall semester only.
We have open volunteer roles. To apply, email your resume.
Other RSOs and local groups can team up with ISD to co-host a fundraiser or a Pet-A-Pup style event.
